advances: An actual capwise residual identity under a fixed finite-source convergence setup. It retains support allocations, continuous normal recording on the boundary, and physical rather than normal-tagged volume and section defects.

proof:
The row masses sum to at most the reciprocal of the common source-value lower bound. Select their full and captured weak limits on the common compact set. Multiplication by $L_j$ and convergence give $L\sum_i\nu_i=dm/M$, since $L_j\sum_i\nu_{ij}=dm_j/M_j$ and $dm_j\rightharpoonup dm$. In particular $\int 1/L\,dm<\infty$ and the ordinary full rows are absolutely continuous with respect to mixed volume. On $\{L>0\}$ the cut is null for each such row, since $u\ne0$. Off the limiting plane the membership bits eventually agree locally, and weak convergence with the plane null identifies the ordinary captured row. On $Z$, restriction of the nonnegative captured weak limit gives $\zeta_i^H\le\zeta_i$.

Affineness and the two moments give $\int(A_{ij}-L_j)\,d\rho_{ij}=0$, hence the row is carried by $A_{ij}=L_j$. The same equality persists on $\nu_i$ by uniform convergence. Different continuous slopes can tie only on a volume-null subset of each fiber. It follows that the physical vector measure $\nabla_X\log L_j\,dm_j$ is exactly $M_j\sum_i c_{ij}\nu_{ij}$, and the corresponding ordinary limiting measure is $M\sum_i c_i\nu_i|_{\{L>0\}}=\nabla_X\log L\,dm$. In particular the captured gradient measures converge to $\mathbf 1_H\nabla_X\log L\,dm+M\sum_i c_i\zeta_i^H$.

Fact 33dad4b1da4f3ba2 bounds both the bulk gradient and boundary logarithmic trace uniformly under these contact hypotheses. For each fiber the assumed positive interior limit gives a positive anchor in $K_z^j$ for large $j$. The homothetic sublevel estimate of the moving-section anchor lemma applied in dimension $d$ gives uniform negative-log bulk tails. Bounded truncation of the bulk logs and almost-everywhere convergence of the fiber and cap indicators thus give convergence of the captured bulk log measures to $\mathbf 1_H\log L\,dm$ with no residual.

For each scalar test $\phi$ continuously differentiable in $X$ on a common neighborhood, apply fiberwise Gauss–Green to $\phi\log L_j$ on the captured bodies. On proper cuts the outward unit normal of the new face is $-u_j/|u_j|$. On the inside supporting face the old outward unit normal is $-u_j/|u_j|$ and the body-plus-section fraction is one. On an outside supporting face the outward unit normal is $u_j/|u_j|$ and the body and section fractions are equal, so they cancel on the same side. These are the all-status signs of the allocated rule and give
$$
\int \phi\log L_j\,n\,\alpha_j\,d\eta_j
=\int_{H_j}(\log L_j\,\nabla_X\phi+\phi\nabla_X\log L_j)\,dm_j
 +u_j\int\phi\log L_j\,d\lambda_j.
$$
The rule also covers strict full/empty fibers and interval endpoints. Set $\phi=1$. The trace and gradient bounds and $|u_j|\ge b_*$ bound $|\int\log L_j\,d\lambda_j|$. The section masses are uniformly bounded by the outer radius and $b_*$, and $(\log L_j)_+$ is uniformly bounded. Thus $\int(-\log L_j)_+\,d\lambda_j$ is bounded too.

By the finite-affine zero-face argument in the anchor lemma, $Z$ is surface-null, and it has zero $(d-1)$-area in every cut plane, including a supporting one. For the latter claim the limiting coarea is dominated by section area by the allocation hypothesis. Bounded positive-log weights pass directly. For the negative logs, bounded truncation yields integrability of each ordinary part, and uniform convergence on compact subsets of $\{L>0\}$ identifies it there. Consequently the remaining limit parts are exactly the restrictions to $Z$ and inherit positivity and selected-body domination.

The same allocated identity holds on the limit with $\log(L+\delta)$ for every $\delta>0$. Let $\delta\downarrow0$. In volume, $\nabla_X\log(L+\delta)$ is dominated by $\|\nabla_XL\|_\infty/L$, and the logs are dominated by a constant plus $(-\log L)_+$. On boundary and section, use the ordinary logarithmic integrability just established and the nullity of $Z$. Dominated convergence therefore gives the ordinary limiting allocated identity with $\log L$. Subtract it from the prelimit identity after taking the weak limits. The negative logarithm contributes $-a_H$ on the boundary and $-s_H$ on the section, yielding the displayed sign and flux. Density extends the tests to all continuous physical $\phi$, separately at every base. Complementing leaves the same section fraction and reverses the normal by the two support rules. The boundary bits sum to one, and the captured volume rows sum to the full rows because the prelimit cap plane is volume-null. This proves all complementary identities.

statement:
Let finitely many sampled full-dimensional convex $d$-fibers $K_z^j$ converge in Hausdorff distance to full-dimensional $K_z$. They have common outer and inball bounds. Write $dm_j,dm$ for mixed volume and $M_j,M>0$ for its masses. Use the positive, log-normalized parameters and finite actual contact rows of 33dad4b1da4f3ba2, with common own-source ball radius, bounded maxima and source values bounded below. More explicitly, for each $j$ the finitely many weighted rows are $\nu_{ij}=(\sigma_{ij}/L_j(Y_{ij}))\rho_{ij}$ with $\sigma_{ij}>0$, $\sum_i\sigma_{ij}=1$, $\rho_{ij}$ a probability of barycenter $Y_{ij}$ and $L_j$-mean $L_j(Y_{ij})$, and $\sum_i\nu_{ij}=dm_j/(M_jL_j)$. Assume the sampled parameters admit the representation $L_j=\min_i A_{ij}$ by actual affine touching planes at the respective marks, with coefficientwise limits $A_i$, $L=\min_i A_i$ positive in each limiting fiber interior, and continuous slopes $c_{ij}\to c_i$. Let $Z=\{L=0\}$ on the limiting sampled set. Assume the recorded normal-bundle measures $\eta_j$ converge weakly to the actual limiting normal-bundle measure $\eta$; the normal coordinate $n$ is the exterior continuous unit normal.

Retain an actual cap $H_j=\{a_j\cdot z+u_j\cdot X\ge t_j\}$ with convergent coefficients and $|u_j|\ge b_*>0$. Its actual boundary selector $\alpha_j$ and section measure $\lambda_j$ use full proper-section coarea and consistent supporting allocations. Thus $\alpha_j$ is the strict-side bit off the cut and, on an inside supporting facet, body and section fractions sum to one, while on an outside supporting facet they are equal. The section fraction multiplies $\mathcal H^{d-1}/|u_j|$, with endpoint counting for $d=1$. Assume the joint unweighted limits $\alpha_j\eta_j\rightharpoonup\alpha\eta$, $\lambda_j\rightharpoonup\lambda$ are consistent allocations for the limiting cap $H$ in this same sense.

Along a common weakly converging subsequence, the full body log measure, selected body log measure and section log measure have limits
$$
\begin{aligned}
(-\log L_j)_+\eta_j&\rightharpoonup(-\log L)_+\eta+b,\\
\alpha_j(-\log L_j)_+\eta_j&\rightharpoonup\alpha(-\log L)_+\eta+a_H,\\
(-\log L_j)_+\lambda_j&\rightharpoonup(-\log L)_+\lambda+s_H.
\end{aligned}
$$
Their residuals are carried over $Z$ with $0\le a_H\le b$, $s_H\ge0$. Let $\nu_i$ be the weak limit of $\nu_{ij}$ and let $\zeta_i=\nu_i|_Z$. The weak limits of $\mathbf 1_{H_j}\nu_{ij}$ have ordinary parts $\mathbf 1_H\nu_i|_{\{L>0\}}$ and residuals $0\le\zeta_i^H\le\zeta_i$ on $Z$. With $\pi$ forgetting only the recorded normal, the physical vector-measure identity, fiber by fiber, is
$$
-\pi_*(n\,a_H)=M\sum_i c_i\zeta_i^H-u\,s_H.
$$
For the complementary cap with the same section allocation and body selector $1-\alpha_j$, the two body residuals sum to $b$, the two row residuals sum to $\zeta_i$, and the section residual is the same. The opposite normals cancel the two section terms, giving $-\pi_*(n\,b)=M\sum_i c_i\zeta_i$.
